note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of markedly elevated PSA and MRI findings following a prior biopsy with discordant pathological features.

The patient is a 67-year-old retired carpenter who lives alone and is divorced. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 2/35. He has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia and is not on any active medication. He is an ex-smoker (15 pack-years, quit in 2012) and swims once a week. He has no known allergies. Recent appointments include a pain clinic visit for chronic shoulder pain, biannual dental check-ups, and physiotherapy for lower back pain. He is hard of hearing and prefers written summaries. His PSA trend shows a significant rise from 9.6 ng/mL in June 2023 to 35.0 ng/mL in January 2025, with an intermediate value of 2.7 ng/mL in March 2024.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate is non-palpable with a smooth, symmetric contour, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of acute distress.
